S293-001 | HIGH | 9/10 | justfile:754
The added bounce safeguard synthesizes a default/named tmux socket path and invokes explicit -S. This skips tmux's native socket-directory ownership validation. Another UID can precreate an absent victim socket directory with an accessible listener; the new client connects and transmits the bounce process's exported environment, potentially including credentials.

This is source-verified against official tmux 3.6a at commit cc117b5048f77a4842820f8ebbe3a86e5c077224:
- tmux.c:211-228: make_label checks the directory owner and permissions.
- tmux.c:428-430,518-534: explicit -S sets path and bypasses make_label.
- client.c:103-181,365-367,487-492: connects, sends/flushed identification, and transmits environment entries.
- proc.c:300-324: getpeereid records the peer UID but does not reject a foreign UID.

Upstream source addresses:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/cc117b5048f77a4842820f8ebbe3a86e5c077224/tmux.c
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/cc117b5048f77a4842820f8ebbe3a86e5c077224/client.c
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/cc117b5048f77a4842820f8ebbe3a86e5c077224/proc.c

The live-old-daemon predicate establishes an HTTP listener, not a victim-owned tmux directory. Planting can precede daemon startup: native tmux refuses the planted directory while the daemon can remain running; bounce then reaches the newly added unsafe connection. An existing private, victim-owned directory prevents this planting attack. This crosses user accounts and is outside C33's same-user exemption.

Required repair: preserve native resolution and validation. Use quoted -L "$PIJ_TMUX_SERVER" for a named server; otherwise let tmux choose inherited TMUX/default itself. Do not synthesize these sockets into -S. The R2 deadline repair alone does not stop this disclosure.

Other reviewed surfaces and limits:
- The security review reports 38 isolated literal-argv/socket-precedence cases and two missing/failing-tmux cases passing; no shell payload execution. Quoting is not the blocker.
- No added credential literals, private owner/name references, or machine-specific home paths were found in the added-lines review.
- The HTTP drain is source-bounded to five seconds with a watch-close drop path. Runtime ordering, store-cancellation safety, client EOF behavior and mutations remain the correctness reviewer's evidence, not additional local security runtime claims.
- The correctness reviewer separately reproduced the unbounded pre-SIGINT tmux call on a stopped private server: pending beyond 2.010 seconds with no signal marker, completing after resume. It remains an R2 availability issue; fixing it does not resolve S293-001.
- Bounce derives its safeguard socket/executable from the caller, not the old daemon's startup environment. This is a targeting limitation, not a separately proven disclosure or session-loss finding.
- The safeguard is a one-directional safety interlock (brake), not a retention policy. Its tmux launch occurs once per bounce, not per seat/tick; performance owns the fleet cost receipts.
